chunks: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who forgets to perform ghusl on the day of Eid until he has prayed. He said: If it is still within the time, then he must perform ghusl and repeat the salat (prayer); but if the time has passed, then his salat (prayer) is valid.

The proper way to understand this report is that it indicates a form of recommendation, because we have already clarified that the ghusl of the two Eids is sunnah (prophetic tradition). We also discussed this fully in the chapter on ghusl in our major book, and we have also clarified that whoever misses the salat (prayer) of the two Eids has no qada' upon him; rather, it is only recommended for him to pray individually.

key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: a recommended prophetic practice, not an obligation
key_terms.غُسْلَ الْعِيدَيْنِ: the ritual bath associated with the two Eids

ai.seo_question: If someone forgets the ghusl of Eid and prays, must he repeat the Eid prayer?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on one who forgets the ghusl of Eid until after performing the Eid prayer. The apparent instruction to repeat the prayer within its time is interpreted by the compiler as a recommendation, since the ghusl of the two Eids is sunnah (prophetic tradition), not obligatory, and missed Eid prayer is not made up as qada'.
